name: transcripts
comment: The 2026-08-26 pass's baseline app: plain WSGI, src/ layout (--app-dir src, the shadowing case), allauth, and a DevAutoLoginMiddleware that logs every request in as admin@transcripts.local under DEBUG -- so there is no login block and no `auth` routes; everything is authenticated. Serve with the checkout's venv on PATH and --cwd at the checkout: `m0serve transcript_manager.wsgi --app-dir src`. Needs one Student row (id 1); its own `init_data` seeder fails on the NOT NULL owner (see the design doc), so create one through the ORM. The PDF, CSV and XLSX exports are byte-deterministic across requests and are the CPU + generated-file rows. No static route: under this settings module /static/ is served only by runserver (no WhiteNoise, no static() urlpattern), so gunicorn and m0serve both 404 it -- an app note, not a server difference.

routes.comment: openpyxl stamps docProps/core.xml with the creation second, so the bytes differ every second (289 digests in one run); fetched for its CPU and its 200, not compared
PDF rendered per request by typst: the CPU-bound generated-file row. No byte count -- the size varies by process (subset fonts), the normalised digest is the assertion

comment_body_sub: The PDF export (typst) stamps /CreationDate and /ModDate, the same dates in its XMP block, and a per-render /ID; each pattern is bounded by its own closer and passes the blinding lint. Measured: two renders differ in exactly those regions. typst also tags each subsetted font with a six-letter prefix that is constant within one server process and differs across processes: one worker matched gunicorn's capture 2,840 times, four workers gave four tags.
